memos.headline: GOOGL and CAT Lead on Relative Strength; MSFT Oversold but Broken; UNH Structurally Damaged
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. GOOGL is sitting at its 52-week high with RSI 68 and extraordinary relative strength vs SPY (+18% over 4w, +40% over 12w), while CAT is +56% over 26 weeks and +25% relative strength over 12 weeks — both are textbook momentum leaders I want to own. On the weak side, MSFT has an RSI of 28.1 and is nearly 8% below its 50-day mean with -7.1% relative strength over 4 weeks, which looks like a breakdown rather than a buyable dip given the deteriorating 12-week trend of -7.4%. UNH is the most structurally damaged name here: trading 47.6% below its 52-week high and 13.7% below its 200-day mean, this is a secular downtrend I want no part of. AAPL remains the cleanest large-cap trend, just 1.4% off its high with balanced RSI at 59.7 and strong relative strength.

views.note: At 52-week highs with RSI 68 and dominant relative strength (+40% vs SPY over 12w); would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~263).
Only 1.4% off highs, RSI 59.7 is healthy, +15.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12w; would cut below the 50-day mean (~259).
Massive 26w return of +56% with +25% relative strength over 12w and RSI 53 leaving room to run; risk is a close below 520.
Quiet uptrend above both moving averages with balanced RSI 53, but relative strength vs SPY is only modestly positive and 26w return of +10% is unremarkable.
RSI 28 is oversold but the 4w return of -9.8% and -7.1% relative strength signal a breakdown; would reconsider only on a reclaim above the 50-day mean (~513).
Down 47.6% from 52-week high and 13.7% below 200-day mean — this is a secular downtrend, not a dip; no level to buy until price reclaims the 200-day.
Still well above 200-day mean (+17%) but 13.6% drawdown and negative 4w/12w relative strength suggest consolidation; need a reclaim of 186 to get constructive.
RSI 40.6 and -13.1% drawdown with weak 12w relative strength (-6.3% vs SPY) keep me sidelined; a close above 228 would improve the picture.
Mild pullback to RSI 40 with 200-day support intact (+7.2% above), but 12w relative strength is slightly negative; watching 290 as support.
Trading 5.4% below its 200-day mean and 16% off highs with negative 12w and 26w returns — a persistent downtrend in a defensive name is a red flag.

memos.headline: NVDA's 56% Net Margin and 62% Revenue Growth Dominate; UNH Earnings Collapse Demands Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest earnings power in NVDA, which just printed $57.01B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a staggering 56.0% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt — this is the best combination of growth, profitability, and balance sheet strength in the universe. GOOGL and MSFT also stand out with 34.2% and 35.7% net margins respectively, both growing revenue double-digits (15.9% and 18.4% YoY) on modest leverage. On the other end, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on $113.16B of revenue, compressing net margin to just 2.1% while carrying $80.14B in debt — I cannot pay for that earnings trajectory until I see margin stabilization. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% with net income down 12.3%, reflecting commodity headwinds that may persist, and CAT's 6.7% net income decline despite 9.5% revenue growth signals margin pressure I want to watch before committing.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, and minimal $8.47B debt make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe; a sustained margin decline below 45% would change my view.
$102.35B revenue growing 15.9% YoY with 34.2% net margin and only $14.79B debt is durable, high-quality earnings power at low leverage.
18.4% revenue growth to $77.67B with 35.7% net margin and manageable $43.21B debt; net income growth of 12.5% lagging revenue growth slightly but margin level is elite.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4% YoY) with net margin expanding to 11.8% and net income up 38.2% shows operating leverage kicking in; I'd reassess if margins compress back below 8%.
Revenue growth of 7.9% is modest and $90.68B in total debt is the highest in the tech cohort; the 86.4% net income jump likely reflects a tough prior-year comp rather than sustainable acceleration.
Solid 31% net margin and 11.6% net income growth, but $427.2B in total debt and cyclical exposure to credit quality keep me at neutral until I see the rate environment stabilize.
Defensive 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but 3% revenue growth limits upside and $24.32B debt is meaningful relative to the revenue base.
Net income down 61.2% YoY to $2.35B with net margin collapsing to 2.1% on $80.14B of debt is a clear cash-flow compression signal; I need to see margin recovery above 4% before reconsidering.
Revenue declining 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin reflects commodity price headwinds; would reconsider on sustained revenue stabilization.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, implying margin compression to 13.0%; I want to see cost discipline restore earnings leverage before turning constructive.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Late-Cycle Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone. However, headline CPI is running at 3.0% y/y (Sep print), which limits the pace of further cuts and keeps real rates elevated. The labor market is softening meaningfully: unemployment at 4.40% is up 30bp over both three and twelve months, consistent with a late-cycle slowdown rather than outright recession. The 10y-2y spread has re-steepened to +55bp from +10bp a year ago, confirming the curve has normalized, while the 10y yield at 4.06% (down 37bp y/y) suggests the bond market is pricing moderate growth deceleration. My regime call is 'easing into slowdown' — duration-sensitive growth should benefit from falling yields, banks face margin pressure from a flatter front end, cyclicals are vulnerable to weakening demand, and staples offer relative safety. A CPI print breaking above 3.5% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would force me to revisit this framework.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits from falling 10y yields and easing cycle; quality balance sheet provides late-cycle resilience.
Lower long-end rates support valuations for high-duration equities, though consumer softening from rising unemployment is a modest headwind.
Defensive staples outperform in late-cycle slowdowns; rising unemployment and easing policy historically favor this sector.
Steeper curve is a positive, but ongoing rate cuts compress NIM on the front end and rising unemployment raises credit loss provisions.
Classic cyclical facing headwinds from softening labor market and late-cycle demand deceleration; 3% CPI limits fiscal stimulus room.
Energy is a macro wildcard — slowdown dampens demand expectations, but supply dynamics are outside my framework; no strong directional call.
Falling yields and easing cycle favor high-growth, long-duration names; secular AI demand partially insulates from cyclical slowdown.
Defensive characteristics are appealing in a slowdown, but healthcare policy uncertainty and sticky medical inflation temper conviction.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: AMZN and CAT Surged While NVDA and MSFT Sold Off — Positioning Implications
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) saw outsized positive reactions to their Q3 results, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have legs, though three weeks later some of that enthusiasm is likely priced. NVDA's -3.2% drop on its 11/19 earnings print is the freshest data point and signals that even strong results are meeting elevated expectations — a classic crowded-positive-tone warning. MSFT's -2.9% post-earnings fade and AAPL's flat -0.4% reaction suggest lukewarm sentiment that hasn't deteriorated enough to be contrarian yet. JPM's -1.9% earnings-day decline and subsequent quiet filing flow point to a market that has already digested the news without conviction either way.

views.note: The +9.6% earnings reaction was the strongest in the universe and the 11/20 follow-on 8-K suggests continued corporate activity, though three weeks of drift may have absorbed some upside.
A -3.2% sell-the-news reaction just yesterday on earnings signals crowded positive positioning meeting reality; sentiment needs to reset before I'd get constructive.
The +11.6% earnings pop was the largest single-day move in the universe, but it is now three weeks old and likely largely priced — I hold modest conviction the narrative shift persists.
A -2.9% post-earnings decline combined with a board-level change filing suggests unsettled sentiment without a clear catalyst to reverse it near-term.
The -0.4% earnings reaction is essentially flat — no narrative shift in either direction, leaving me without a sentiment edge.
The -1.9% earnings-day dip and subsequent routine filings suggest the market has moved on; no tone inflection to trade.
A muted +0.2% earnings reaction and a flurry of routine 8-Ks signal stable but uninspiring sentiment — no edge here.
The +0.5% earnings reaction was tepid and subsequent filings (Reg FD, bylaws amendment) don't indicate a sentiment shift worth trading.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Surging VIX Signal Structural Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am writing with the VIX at 26.42, up 45% over one month and nearly 70% over three months, while the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 312.65—down modestly month-over-month but up 76% over three months, indicating a structurally elevated policy-risk regime rather than a one-off spike. High-yield OAS has widened 23 bps over three months to 3.17%, confirming that credit markets are beginning to price geopolitical and policy tail risk. WTI crude at $60.07 is down 6.4% over three months despite a modest monthly bounce, suggesting demand-side concerns (possibly sanctions/tariff-related slowdown fears) are outweighing supply disruption premia. I have highest conviction on names with concentrated China/export-control exposure (NVDA, AAPL) and lowest conviction on domestically oriented defensives (PG, UNH) where policy risk is more diffuse; a material de-escalation in US-China trade tensions or a rollback of semiconductor export controls would change my view on the tech names.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls to China remain the single largest structural geopolitical overhang; the 76% 3m surge in policy uncertainty and elevated VIX reinforce that this risk is not yet fully discounted.
Heavy supply-chain concentration in China and rising policy uncertainty create ongoing tariff and production-disruption risk that the current vol environment underscores.

WTI at $60 reflects demand weakness despite geopolitical supply risks; four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate repositioning, but I lack clarity on whether energy-security tailwinds offset macro headwinds.
CAT's global infrastructure exposure makes it vulnerable to trade-policy disruption; the elevated uncertainty index and widening HY spreads suggest downstream capex could slow.

Domestic consumer staples offer relative shelter from geopolitical shocks; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest proactive disclosure, and the name's low beta to trade-policy risk is attractive in this regime.
Widening HY spreads and a flat-ish 10y-2y curve at 55 bps limit upside, but JPM's diversified franchise and recent Reg FD disclosures suggest manageable geopolitical exposure.
Cloud and enterprise software have moderate China exposure relative to hardware peers; policy uncertainty is a headwind but less direct than for NVDA or AAPL.
Antitrust and regulatory risk are the primary geopolitical vectors; the elevated uncertainty index warrants caution but the threat is more regulatory than trade-war driven.

Avoid UNH, MSFT, and PG where analyst views are conflicted or structurally negative.

Geopolitics analyst is neutral on regulatory risk but not bearish. Best risk/reward in the universe.
